userStories.title: Async coalesced atomic persistence
userStories.description: As a user, I want typing not to block on a full disk write so that the editor stays responsive and a crash cannot corrupt my state.
acceptanceCriteria: All 83 persistLocked() call sites replaced with a.markDirty(scope)
A single background writer goroutine coalesces on a ~250 ms debounce
Force-flush on beforeClose, shutdown, and window blur
json.Marshal replaces json.MarshalIndent

userStories.notes: markDirty(scope) replaces 80 persistLocked() call sites; background writer, debounce 250ms + lastWriteDuration (a fixed interval would let the writer monopolise a.mu, which persistLocked holds for its whole ~82ms duration). Atomic writeFileAtomic: temp in same dir, Chmod, Write, Sync, checked Close, Rename. json.Marshal replaces MarshalIndent. VERIFIED BY ORCHESTRATOR: BenchmarkMarkDirty 573,933 ns/op / 3,354 B/op vs the 225,684,108 ns / 221,066,295 B keystroke baseline = 393x faster, 65,900x fewer bytes. persistLocked itself 225.7ms -> 81.1ms. Gates: build 0, vet 0, test 32.897s 0, race 63.130s clean, golangci-lint 0. Test count 474 -> 483. Kill-mid-write proven: TestPersistStateJSONSurvivesSIGKILL re-execs the binary, SIGKILLs at 8 offsets, parses after each; worker demonstrated BOTH durability tests FAIL against the old os.WriteFile writer. Write errors: dirty flag stays set (retry, backoff to 5s), parked in a.persistErr and returned by the next markDirty (which has a caller), notification on first failure of a streak only, plus log. ACCEPTED REGRESSION: PersistLockedSmallState 542us -> 5.5ms, entirely the mandated fsync (~4.7ms on APFS); kept deliberately for durability - see .ralph/baseline/bench.txt. FOLLOW-UPS: blur flush needs FlushPendingWrites bound in regenerated frontend/wailsjs (out of scope); 21 persistLocked calls remain sync by design (3 bootstrap in ensureReadyLocked, 2 rollback function values, 16 in recovery/draft/import/git outside scope); persistLocked still holds a.mu for the whole write - getting I/O off the mutex belongs with US-020.

userStories.notes: 21 built-in shim sources compiled once behind sync.Once and run via RunProgram. Verified by orchestrator on the US-005 host: 10x = 813,946 ns/op (target <=1,094,673); steady state 1000x x3 = 443k..535k ns/op vs 5,473,367 baseline, ~10x. Allocations 66,119 -> 8,070 (8.2x), bytes 4,049,912 -> 701,050 (5.8x) - deterministic across every run, which is the honest signal here. Gates: build 0, vet 0, test 23.497s 0, race 38.398s clean, golangci-lint 0. Test count 468 -> 474. Uses sync.Once rather than the story's sync.OnceValue: OnceValue needs a niladic func, and all 21 sources are function-local literals, 8 of them mid-function; hoisting ~15,000 lines of JS to package scope would have been an unreviewable diff for zero gain. CORRECTS THE ORCHESTRATOR'S BRIEFING: the eager/lazy split was wrong. installScriptRequire (app.go:17680) eagerly builds the entire module table regardless of what the user script require()s, so ALL 21 are eager - 15 in safe mode (the benchmark's mode), 6 more in developer mode, worth a further 1.77 ms/runtime there.

userStories.description: As a user, I want variable substitution to scale with body size rather than with variable count so that large bodies interpolate quickly.

userStories.notes: Single left-to-right scan + strings.Builder. CORRECTED FIGURES: steady state (-benchtime=200000x -count=3) vars=50 = 647..669 ns/op vs 14,583 baseline, i.e. ~22x, allocations 29 -> 1, bytes 13,609 -> 320. An earlier 875 ns/op (16.7x) figure was a single -benchtime=10x sample; 10x is too noisy for code this fast (15 samples spanned 708..1554 ns, straddling the 1458 ns acceptance threshold). See the methodology warning in .ralph/baseline/bench.txt. Semantics pinned by a 36-case characterisation suite written against the OLD implementation and verified to pass against BOTH (worker restored the original app.go and re-ran it). KNOWN BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: nesting depth is now deterministically 8 substitutions. The old per-key ReplaceAll loop could collapse deeper chains when Go's map order was lucky - an 11-link chain returned END 198/200 runs and {{v10}} 2/200. New returns {{v8}} every time. Chains needing <=8 substitutions are unaffected. Old cyclic handling was also nondeterministic (a growing cycle produced 12 distinct outputs over 200 runs); new is deterministic. Gates: build 0, vet 0, test 25.560s 0, race 44.222s clean, golangci-lint 0. Test count 461 -> 468.
